text_blocks.snippet: The most common autoimmune diseases include rheumatoid arthritis, type 1 diabetes, multiple sclerosis, lupus, Crohn's disease, psoriasis, and Hashimoto's thyroiditis. These conditions affect a significant number of people and are characterized by the immune system mistakenly attacking the body's own healthy tissues.
snippet_highlighted_words: rheumatoid arthritis, type 1 diabetes, multiple sclerosis, lupus, Crohn's disease, psoriasis, and Hashimoto's thyroiditis

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a bit more detail on some of the most common ones:

list.title: Rheumatoid Arthritis:
list.snippet: This disease primarily affects the joints, causing pain, swelling, and stiffness.

list.title: Type 1 Diabetes:
list.snippet: In this condition, the immune system attacks the insulin-producing cells in the pancreas, leading to the body's inability to regulate blood sugar.

list.title: Multiple Sclerosis:
list.snippet: This neurological disease affects the brain and spinal cord, causing a range of symptoms like muscle weakness, vision problems, and fatigue.

list.title: Lupus:
list.snippet: Lupus is a systemic disease that can affect various organs and tissues, including the skin, joints, kidneys, and brain.
